thread:
maya_support: Hey — customer (acme-inc) reports a 403 when switching projects in the Console after an IdP maintenance window. Error shown: 'You don't have permission to view this project (403)'. They can still call model APIs with their org api-key. Any ideas?

jordan_se: Got repro steps?

maya_support: Copied from customer:
1) Login via SSO
2) Click org dropdown -> switch to 'acme-prod'
3) Console shows 403; API calls with api-key succeed
4) IdP session rekey/rotation happened ~3h ago.
Screenshot: https://acme.screenshot/snap.png

alex_sre: Likely a group-claim / session-binding issue — could be delegated token lost console scopes. Can you gather authz trace id when they hit the console?

idp-bot: IdP notice: SAML session rekey for tenant acme-inc at 2026-03-17T07:12:30Z. SCIM last sync: 2026-03-17T07:10:14Z.

jordan_se: If they're using Okta + SCIM, a group rename during rotation can leave our role mappings pointing at the old group name. Ask customer for the token claims or run /self.

maya_support: Asked them to run:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <id_token>" https://console.redwood.ai/v1/self
They returned 403 with body: {"error":"insufficient_scope","scopes":["console:view"]} — so token missing console scopes.

alex_sre: That looks like the token lost the console:view/group claims — two possibilities: (1) token issued before SCIM rename and mapping is stale, or (2) proxy started honoring delegated session with narrower scopes after rotation. Ask them to re-auth via SSO and/or try incognito. Also request authz log for trace-9853.

leslie_csm: Customer is on Dedicated and needs admin access to unblock billing edits. This is urgent if workaround takes >1h.

maya_support: They tried hard refresh + incognito + full re-login, still 403.

alex_sre: I'm pulling our authz logs for project=acme-prod user=j.park@acme.com. Found failure: missing group claim 'acme-prod-admins' in token. SCIM history shows group renamed to 'acme-prod-admins-v2' at 07:09Z. Our role mapping is still bound to the old name. Root cause: SCIM rename + session rekey produced tokens without the expected group name.

jordan_se: Short-term workaround: org admin can either remap the new SCIM group to the project role (Console > Org settings > Role mappings) or add the affected user directly to the project owner role. Long-term we should accept group aliases or add a tolerant mapping. Opening internal INF-6123.

maya_support: Sent steps to customer: (1) org admin add user to Project Owners via UI (2) trigger SCIM resync in IdP or re-map group (3) user re-login. Customer did step 1 and confirmed immediate write access restored.

leslie_csm: Marking P1 until they confirm billing edit restored. I'll coordinate with account team for communication.

idp-bot: Auto-note: SCIM resync triggered by support at 2026-03-17T08:01:05Z.

maya_support: Closing loop — customer confirmed console write perms and billing tab restored after org admin direct add + re-login. Patch INF-6123 will reduce recurrence. :white_check_mark:
